title: _normalise_frontier_range_pair silently accepts booleans as range bounds (e.g. [False, True] -> (0.0, 1.0)) on the config path, inconsistent with the sibling _reject_bool_chunk_size policy
description: Because bool is a subclass of int, float(False)==0.0 and float(True)==1.0, and booleans pass the finiteness and ordering checks. So a frontier-range value of [False, True] (or {'min': False, 'max': True}) is silently normalised to the numeric range (0.0, 1.0) instead of being rejected as a malformed payload. This is the opposite policy from the file's own sibling validator _reject_bool_chunk_size (lines 21-24), which was deliberately added to reject bool for streaming_chunk_size on the grounds that a bool is almost certainly a client bug rather than a real number. As with finding 1, the request-body path (OptimiserFrontierRequest.threshold_ranges, list[float]) is unaffected because pydantic coerces [False,True] to [0.0,1.0] before the after-validator runs; the silent acceptance is reachable on the config-side path (_auto_frontier_ranges_from_config) where raw JSON booleans flow straight in. Severity is low because boolean range bounds in an optimiser config are a degenerate, low-probability input, but it is a genuine validation gap and an inconsistency with the module's stated bool-rejection stance for numeric fields.
evidence: Runtime: `_normalise_frontier_range_pair([False, True], field='x')` returns (0.0, 1.0); `_normalise_frontier_range_pair({'min': False, 'max': True}, field='x')` returns (0.0, 1.0). No isinstance(..., bool) guard exists in the function, whereas the adjacent _reject_bool_chunk_size (line 22) does `if isinstance(value, bool): raise ValueError(...)`. isinstance(True, int) is True, so the int-based float() coercion accepts bools.
